children: FireFly Robotics filed a Form S-1 for a direct listing on the Nasdaq Global Market under the proposed ticker FFLY. The company registered up to 27,134,738 shares of common stock for resale by existing stockholders and will not receive proceeds from those sales. The listing is not underwritten; Chardan Capital Markets will act as financial advisor for the Nasdaq opening process.

FireFly Robotics is an agricultural technology company focused on autonomous and semi-autonomous turf care equipment. The company designs and manufactures its products in the U.S. and sells directly to customers, combining hardware, software, services, and parts under a vertically integrated model. FireFly’s Autonomous Mowing Platform (AMP) includes the AMP‑L100 reel mower for fairways and the AMP‑X100 rotary mower for longer cuts, each powered by an all‑electric drivetrain and a full autonomy stack using LiDAR, cameras, AI/ML, and RTK‑corrected GPS. Its manned robotic harvester (MRH) line serves turf farms with diesel‑electric hybrids that automate cutting and palletizing to reduce labor and fuel usage.

The company complements hardware with software and data services, including its FireLink fleet management application and Mercury performance data platform, plus a nationwide service team and parts business. FireFly markets directly to golf courses, sports fields, municipalities, and turf farms. In 2025, revenue mix was approximately 54% MRH sales, 20% parts, 16% AMPs, 1% subscription software, and 9% other.
: Company estimates a combined TAM of approximately $60 billion across golf, precision mowing, and turf harvesting
: Installed base of machines grew from 76 in 2016 to 900+ by June 30, 2026 (CAGR ~29.9%); revenue grew from $11.3M in 2016 to $47.2M in 2025 (CAGR ~17.3%)
: Vertically integrated U.S. manufacturer with first-mover advantage in large-area autonomous electric mowers and manned robotic harvesters
: Deere & Company, The Toro Company, Husqvarna Group, AGCO, CNH Industrial, CLAAS, Kubota, Mahindra, Jacobsen, Trebro, Kesmac
: Electrification, labor shortages, autonomy/AI adoption, sustainability and emissions reduction, and noise-reduction enabling extended mowing hours
: AMPs are operating at over 75 country clubs as of mid‑2026; MRH deployed across numerous turf farms globally
: 108,500 sq. ft. facility in Salt Lake City, Utah; direct-to-customer sales and service
: U.S., Australia, Canada, Mexico, U.K., Brazil, South Africa, Israel; growing international footprint
: Chardan Capital Markets serving as financial advisor for the Nasdaq listing process
: AMP order backlog of 76 units as of June 30, 2026

: 900+ machines (AMP, MRH, M220) in service worldwide; ~130 AMPs delivered by June 30, 2026; AMPs have autonomously mowed over 100,000 acres; 17 U.S. service technicians and 2 international; 213 employees as of June 30, 2026; MRH fleet capacity ~10,750 turf pallets/day
, Chief Executive Officer and Director - Former executive at ProFire Energy; experience in public company leadership, strategy, and finance.
, Chief Technology Officer and Chairman - Mechanical engineer with nearly three decades in automation; prior roles at AAI Textron, National Instruments, and Honda R&D.
, President and Chief Operating Officer - Co‑founder with 20+ years of operational leadership across agriculture, technology, and services.
, Chief Financial Officer - CPA; prior CFO roles at TruGolf and Xevant; extensive private and public company finance experience.
: Up to 27,134,738 shares of common stock registered for resale in a direct listing
: None (direct listing; Chardan Capital Markets as financial advisor)
: The company will not receive any proceeds from the sale of shares by the Registered Stockholders.
